images.author: CDC / Dr. Fred Murphy
images.why: Digitally colourised, negative-stain TEM of a cluster of actual smallpox viruses; catalogued as variola. Best confirmed colour match. Linked JPEG is the preview; the page offers a 19.52 MB high-resolution download whose direct URL could not be verified.

images.author: John Gallagher and Audray Harris, NIAID Laboratory of Infectious Diseases
images.why: Colourised TEM of red-and-gold influenza A/H3N2 spherical virions, from a strain isolated in Victoria, Australia, in 1975. Strong colour contrast. Flickr large-rendition URL; original resolution and download availability could not be verified.

images.author: John Gallagher and Audray Harris, NIAID Laboratory of Infectious Diseases
images.why: Colourised TEM explicitly identifying blue influenza A/H1N1 particles. Flickr large-rendition URL; original resolution and download availability could not be verified.

images.author: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
images.why: Digitally colourised TEM showing a small grouping of H1N1 influenza particles. Compact subject grouping is promising for a 9:10 crop. Linked JPEG is the preview; the page offers an 8.85 MB high-resolution download.

images.source: NIH / NIGMS full-quality file; NIH Image Gallery on Flickr for caption and licence
images.author: Seth Pincus, Elizabeth Fischer and Austin Athman, NIAID/NIH
images.why: Caption identifies yellow HIV attacking a blue human T cell. Excellent contrasting colours and detailed cell texture. NIGMS supplies this same image as a 3.9 MB full-quality JPEG; pixel dimensions were not verified.

images.author: NIAID/NIH, Integrated Research Facility, Fort Detrick
images.why: TEM explicitly showing red/yellow HIV-1 particles budding from a blue/teal chronically infected H9 cell, including immature and mature virions. Flickr large-rendition URL; original resolution and download availability could not be verified.
